premise: Choosing to test his polio vaccine on himself and his own family before mass clinical trials.
hook: The polio epidemic terrified the world, and millions waited anxiously for a breakthrough while children filled iron lungs.
key_facts: Developed the first successful inactivated polio vaccine in the early 1950s.
Inoculated himself, his wife, and his children to prove the vaccine's safety prior to the 1954 trials.
Refused to patent the vaccine, asking 'Would you patent the sun?'
Field trials involving 1.8 million children proved the vaccine safe and effective in 1955.

premise: Working as a master carpenter in Hollywood while struggling to get cast in major film roles.
hook: Before he flew the Millennium Falcon, he built cabinets for George Lucas and was told he would never make it as an actor.
key_facts: Moved to Los Angeles in 1964 and signed a weekly contract with Columbia Pictures.
Became a self-taught carpenter to support his wife and two young sons when acting work dried up.
Built a recording studio for Sergio Mendes and cabinets for Francis Ford Coppola.
Hired by George Lucas to build a doorway, which directly led to his audition for Star Wars.

premise: Keeping his entire 28-man crew alive for nearly two years after their ship was crushed by Antarctic ice.
hook: Their ship was trapped, crushed, and sunk, leaving them stranded on floating ice packs a thousand miles from civilization.
key_facts: The Endurance became trapped in pack ice in the Weddell Sea in 1915.
After the ship sank, the crew camped on floating ice floes for months.
Shackleton and five men made an 800-mile journey in a 22-foot lifeboat to South Georgia Island for rescue.
Every single member of the Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition survived.

premise: Working as a bus conductor in Bangalore before rising to become one of Indian cinema's biggest superstars.
hook: He handed out tickets on Bangalore city buses while dreaming of the stage.
key_facts: Worked various jobs including carpentry and as a Bangalore Transport Service bus conductor.
Acted in amateur plays, notably mythological roles in Kannada productions.
Joined the Film and Television Institute of Madras in 1973 to study acting.
Made his cinematic debut in K. Balachander's Tamil film Apoorva Raangangal in 1975.

premise: Accepting the perilous Vostok 1 assignment, knowing the mission's safety systems had barely been tested.
hook: He climbed into a cramped metal sphere atop a ballistic missile, becoming the first human launched into the unknown.
key_facts: Selected from a group of 20 Soviet Air Force fighter pilots for the Vostok program.
Flew aboard Vostok 1 on April 12, 1961, completing one orbit of Earth.
Ejected from the spacecraft at 20,000 feet as per the standard landing design of the time.
Became an international celebrity and hero following the successful historic flight.

premise: Inventing a revolutionary tactile reading system as a teenager after losing his sight in a childhood accident.
hook: Blinded at age three by an awl in his father's harness shop, he spent his youth fighting for the right to read.
key_facts: Blinded in his left eye by an accident and subsequently lost sight in both eyes due to sympathetic ophthalmia.
Entered the Royal Institution for Blind Youth in Paris in 1819.
Adapted Captain Charles Barbier's 'night writing' military code into a six-dot cell system.
Published the system in 1829, allowing blind individuals to read and write efficiently.

premise: Inventing the microwave oven after a candy bar melted in his pocket while standing near a magnetron.
hook: A physicist working on radar technology noticed a peanut cluster melting in his pocket and realized military tech could cook food.
key_facts: Self-taught engineer who worked for Raytheon, becoming a leading expert in radar design.
Stood in front of an active magnetron tube during wartime research in 1945.
Noticed his peanut butter candy bar had liquefied.
Patented the microwave oven in 1945, with the first commercial model appearing in 1947.

premise: Overcoming orphanhood and severe scalp ailments to build a cosmetics empire and become America's first self-made female millionaire.
hook: Suffering from hair loss due to poor sanitation and lack of indoor plumbing, she formulated her own healing tonic.
key_facts: Born on a cotton plantation in Delta, Louisiana, orphaned at age seven.
Worked for decades as a washerwoman before developing hair care products for Black women.
Founded Madam C.J. Walker Manufacturing Company in 1906.
Employed thousands of women as sales agents and became a prominent philanthropist.

premise: Choosing to disobey protocol and report a nuclear warning signal as a false alarm during the height of the Cold War.
hook: Computer screens flashed with incoming US ballistic missiles, and he had minutes to decide whether to launch a retaliatory strike.
key_facts: Served as a lieutenant colonel in the Soviet Air Defense Forces in 1983.
The Oko nuclear early warning system falsely reported five American missiles launched from Montana.
Suspected a computer malfunction because the incoming count was too low for a first strike.
Reported the alert as a false alarm, averting a potential nuclear exchange.

premise: Climbing to the roof of the world alongside Edmund Hillary after years of working as a high-altitude porter.
hook: He carried heavy loads for foreign expeditions for decades before finally standing on the summit of Mount Everest.
key_facts: Born in Tibet and grew up in Nepal as part of the Sherpa community.
Participated in multiple Everest expeditions throughout the 1930s and 1940s as a sirdar and porter.
Reached the summit of Everest with Edmund Hillary on May 29, 1953.
Named one of Time magazine's 100 most influential people of the 20th century.

premise: Inventing a uniquely 'failed' low-tack adhesive that spent years looking for a purpose until a colleague needed a bookmark.
hook: He created an adhesive that stuck lightly to surfaces without leaving residue, and everyone thought it was utterly useless.
key_facts: Worked as a chemist at 3M developing stronger adhesives for aerospace applications in 1968.
Created a pressure-sensitive acrylate copolymer microsphere adhesive that could be repositioned.
Hosted internal seminars for five years trying to find an application for the sticky substance.
Colleague Art Fry used the adhesive in 1974 to anchor bookmarks in his church hymnal, leading to the Post-it Note.

premise: Deciding to fly a single-engine monoplane across the treacherous Atlantic Ocean without a parachute or radio.
hook: He stripped his custom aircraft of every ounce of excess weight—including the radio—to bet his life on a nonstop flight to Paris.
key_facts: Flew the custom-built Spirit of St. Louis from Roosevelt Field, New York, to Paris in May 1927.
Completed the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight in 33.5 hours.
Flew without a forward-facing windshield, relying on a periscope to see ahead.
Became an instant global aviation icon upon landing at Le Bourget Airport.

premise: Inventing the chocolate chip cookie because she ran out of baker's chocolate and substituted chopped Nestlé semi-sweet bars.
hook: She expected the chocolate chunks to melt into the batter during baking, but instead, they held their shape to create a culinary revolution.
key_facts: Owned and operated the Toll House Inn in Whitman, Massachusetts, during the 1930s.
Baked butter drop cookies for her guests in 1938 using chopped Nestlé chocolate bars.
Struck a deal with Nestlé in 1939 to print her recipe on product packaging in exchange for a lifetime supply of chocolate.
Created one of the most popular dessert recipes in American history by accident.
